title: An evening with Raza Ali Khan organised by All Pakistan Music Conference
description:
Visiting maestro, Ustad Raza Ali Khan is the custodian of Kasur-Patiala gharana’s illustrious legacy. The son of Ustad Munawwar Ali Khan & grandson to the indomitable Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan sahib, Ustad Raza Ali Khan inherits a strong, tradition of khayal and thumri from his forefathers.
Ustad Raza Ali Khan received training from Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan until his death and thereafter from his father Ustad Munawar Ali Khan. He started public performance accompanying his father, Ustad Munawwar Ali Khan and gave his first solo recital at the prestigious platform of Eden Garden in Calcutta at the tender age of 15. Encouraged by the reception of this performance, he never looked back and has grown from strength to strength, now counted not only as the foremost exponent of the Kasur-Patiala gharana but also a most revered teacher. Ustad Raza Ali Khan is also part of the ITC Sangeet Research Academy faculty.
Ustad Raza Ali Khan manifests all the defining characteristics of his gharana’s gayeki in his adayegi, use of khatka & gamak, tez sargam and intricate taans in the performances.
Accompanied by Akhtar Hussian Sahib on Harmonium, Sajid Ali on Tabla and Gul Mohammad on Sarangi in his performance

title: Raag Champak (Khayal & Tarana)  -by Ustad Umeed Ali Khan
description:
Raag Champak (Khayal & Tarana)

Ustad Ummeed Ali Khan accompanied by Hamid Hussain (on Sarangi) and Allah Ditta (on Tabla)

*A Syed Wajid's Presentation

Umeed Ali Khan (1910 - 1979)

"Like his father (Ustad Piyare Khan), Umeed Ali Khan was also gifted with sweet, rich, lively and forceful voice, which he dexterously used in the promotion of Gowaliar style of classical singing. Years of hard training under the supervision of his father made Umeed Ali Khan's style highly sophisticated and refined.

"From late 1930s to the middle of 1970s, Ustad Umeed Ali Khan ranked high in the hierarchy of classical vocalists of the sub-continent. He was known for his passion and ability for promoting and popularising the Gwalior gharana style of kheyal singing.

Until his death, Ustad Umeed Ali Khan remained a faithful exponent of the Gowaliar gharana of kheyal singing, a trait which he also passed on to his disciples, including the classical duo of Fateh Ali Khan-Hameed Ali Khan of Hyderabad, Sindh. Another follower of the Gowaliar clan of musicians is composer Master Manzoor Husain.

During his prime, the late Ustad Umeed Ali Khan excelled a number of his contemporaries in the rendition of taranas, thumris and dadras. His mature and deep musical insight were augmented by his refined melodic thinking and acute sensitivity. Handsome vocalist late Ustad Umeed Ali Khan developed a good taste for clothing and living in a style."
